LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.3 Reading for comprehension (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand t
Topic 2.4: Reading aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading aloud, part of Reading 2.3 Reading for comprehension (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand t in Grade 4 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: what they do during the week. What do you like reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise basic punctuation marks for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read words aloud for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. recognise basic punctuation marks for fluency,

   Reading aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read words aloud for fluency,

   Reading aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the role punctuation plays in reading.

   Reading aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read along to a song about days of the week (z.B. Kinderlied "Wochentage" https://www.heilpaedagogik- info.de/kinder-lieder/2573- wochentage.html),

2. read out tongue twisters to peers for feedback (z.B. Am zehnten zehnten zehn Uhr zehn zogen zehn zahme Ziegen zehn Zentner Zucker zum Zoo.),

3. read aloud simple poems on days of the week,

4. read aloud and discuss with peers

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read along to a song about days of the week (z.B. Kinderlied "Wochentage" https://www.heilpaedagogik- info.de/kinder-lieder/2573- wochentage.html),
2. read out tongue twisters to peers for feedback (z.B. Am zehnten zehnten zehn Uhr zehn zogen zehn zahme Ziegen zehn Zentner Zucker zum Zoo.),
3. read aloud simple poems on days of the week,
4. read aloud and discuss with peers

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: The learner develops skills of speaking clearly and effectively as they read aloud

simple poems on days of the week.

Values:
Integrity: The learner observes the rules of doing the right thing at the right time as they read aloud and discuss with

peers what they do during the week.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer pressure: The learner develops awareness of how to handle peer pressure as they read aloud and discuss with peers

what they do during the week.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner links the concept of peer pressure to the concept of decision making in Social Studies. (life skills)
